Officer's narrative
On the reported date, I responded to a rear-end collision on a public roadway in Pasadena, Texas. Driver 1 was
stopped in a travel lane when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 1 stated that neck pain
and stiffness began shortly after impact and reported whilpash symptoms at the scene. Driver 1 presented a policy
card and insurance documents listing Driver 1 as the named insured on the vehicle. Driver 2 acknowledged following
too closely and did not dispute the sequence of events. Two independent witnesses in nearby vehicles gave
statements consistent with Driver 2 striking the rear of the stopped vehicle. Scene photographs show rear-end
damage that is generally consistent with the described impact speed and direction. The vehicle's prior condition
showed no earlier damage that I could identify or that either driver mentioned. A Passenger was present in the front
seat. Driver 1's exact seating position at the moment of impact could not be fully established from statements and
observations at the scene. Both drviers were advised of their reporting obligations, and no citation was issued at this
time.
</page>
